scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Maringa derived from the traditional nkumba dance of the former Kingdom of Loango, which spans parts of today's Republic of the Congo, southern Gabon, and Angola's Cabinda.
During the 1920s to 1940s, it flourished within the urban bar-dancing culture of Brazzaville and Léopoldville.
In the subsequent decades of the 1940s and 1950s, the arrival of Cuban son recordings catalyzed its direct transformation into Congolese rumba.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Early maringa performances incorporated a distinct ensemble consisting of a bass drum, an accordion or likembe (lamellophone), and empty glass bottles struck vertically with spoons to produce percussive accents.
Listen for the bass drum, accordion (likembe), glass bottles.

Early maringa combined the resonant drive of a bass drum with the plucked tones of an accordion or likembe, accented by the sharp clinking of glass bottles struck vertically as percussive instruments.
